extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Department of Education federal financial assistance (K-12 and postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, school administrators, compliance officers, and their legal advisers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements from the Department of Education's final Title IX rule (34 CFR Part 106) describing definitions, recipient obligations, grievance procedures, supportive measures, and other standards institutions must meet to operate free from sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose (§106.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifies scope and purpose of Title IX regulatory amendments to align requirements with Title IX's nondiscrimination mandate and obligations of recipients to provide an educational environment free from discrimination on the basis of sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that regulations apply to recipients (elementary, secondary, postsecondary institutions, and others), and are intended to provide clarity while allowing discretion for variation in institution size and structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Sex-Based Harassment (§106.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines prohibited 'sex-based harassment' and breaks it into categories (quid pro quo, hostile environment) and related concepts (sexual assault, consent, dating/domestic violence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes discussion of data, scope, burden/cost, vagueness/overbreadth concerns, and interplay with other protections; used as the baseline for determining actionable harassment under Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hostile Environment—Davis Standard (§106.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses application of the Davis v. Monroe standard for hostile environment claims under Title IX and considers First Amendment implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses how the Davis standard interacts with tracking, investigating, and enforcing Title IX in schools, including how to reconcile with free-speech and academic freedom concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hostile Environment—Severe or Pervasive; Subjective and Objective Offensiveness (§106.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies that hostile environment harassment is evaluated for severity or pervasiveness and requires both subjective (victim's perception) and objective offensiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists factors to consider (degree of impact; type, frequency, duration; ages/roles/previous interactions; location/context; other sex-based harassment) and addresses online harassment and age/educational-level differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quid Pro Quo Sex-Based Harassment (§106.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifies quid pro quo harassment (conditioning educational benefits on sexual conduct) as a form of sex-based harassment prohibited by Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains examples and that such conduct is actionable regardless of whether it creates a hostile environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Complainant, Complaint, and Respondent (§106.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides regulatory definitions for 'complainant', 'complaint', and 'respondent' to determine who has rights, notice, and procedural protections under the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses rights of complainants and respondents, effect on recipients, and comments requesting broader or narrower definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Title IX and Scope (§106.2; §106.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'Title IX' and clarifies the geographic and substantive scope of sex discrimination covered, including potential coverage for sexual orientation, gender identity, sex characteristics, pregnancy, menstruation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains reliance on Bostock and Title VII case law for scope questions and addresses requests to add specific bases such as menstruation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Relevant' and 'Remedies' (§106.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines what evidence or information is 'relevant' and what constitutes appropriate 'remedies' for victims of sex discrimination under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides how remedies should be prompt and effective and tailored to address the effects of sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and Treatment of Students With Disabilities (§106.2 and §106.8(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'student with a disability' and requires recipients to ensure access to accommodations and auxiliary aids for students with disabilities in Title IX processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers interaction with disability law, postsecondary student issues, and specific training/recordkeeping considerations for accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Definitions (Employee, Recipient, Program or Activity, Federal Financial Assistance, Party, Sex Discrimination) (§106.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Retains, updates, or explains additional statutory/regulatory definitions necessary for administering Title IX obligations and determining applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes discussion of proposed vs final changes and commenters' requests; clarifies which recipients and programs fall under the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application (§106.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishes when and how Title IX applies to conduct—under a recipient's education program or activity, including extraterritorial application and conduct in organizations' buildings or under disciplinary authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses obligations to address conduct occurring under recipients' programs and benefits/burdens for recipients, with attention to free speech and ministerial exception doctrines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Other Requirements and Preservation of Rights (§106.6—FERPA/GEPA interaction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains the interplay between Title IX and other federal requirements, especially FERPA/GEPA, in disclosing information relevant to allegations of sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details how Title IX investigations and disclosures interact with FERPA across different recipient types and regarding students with disabilities, sexual orientation, gender identity, and pregnancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of a Title IX Coordinator (§106.8(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires each recipient to designate a Title IX Coordinator responsible for coordinating compliance and responses to sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies scope of the coordinator role, duties (including monitoring), comprehensive requirements, and responsibilities to ensure prompt and effective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination Policy, Grievance Procedures, Notice of Nondiscrimination (§106.8(b)-(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires recipients to adopt and publish nondiscrimination policies, grievance procedures, and notices describing how to make complaints and available rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses requests to add protected bases, content and publication requirements, and consistency with free-speech/religious exemptions concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Requirements (§106.8(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandates training for relevant individuals on definitions (e.g., sex-based harassment), notification requirements, impartiality, and other topics necessary for fair grievance processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers frequency, who must be trained, the benefits/time/expense tradeoffs, live trainings, and training for decisionmakers (noted in RIA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping (§106.8(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires recipients to keep documentation records, investigative records, training materials, and certain pregnancy-related documents for specified periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes what must be documented and stored, training-material retention, and how recordkeeping interacts with other privacy laws and the regulatory record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty To Address Sex Discrimination (Recipients' Operational Duties) (§106.44(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligates recipients to take prompt and effective steps to address sex discrimination, including notice duties and appropriate monitoring and remediation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers statutory authority, comparison with Title VII/Section 504/IDEA, neutrality of coordinators, and dual-enrollment considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring for Barriers (§106.44(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires recipients to monitor their programs and activities for barriers to reporting or accessing protections against sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses reporting channels, compliance burdens, and free-speech/academic-freedom considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification Requirements (§106.44(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies when and how recipients must notify individuals about sex-discrimination matters, including content and timing of disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses scope, consistency with state laws, disclosures to law enforcement, age-appropriateness, study abroad, employment discrimination intersections, and training implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential Employee Definition and Requirements (§106.44(d) and §106.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'confidential employee' categories (privileged employees; those designated to provide services; employees conducting IRB-approved research) and recipient duties concerning them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must identify confidential employees and understand interactions between confidentiality and grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Awareness Events (§106.44(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses recipients' obligations and considerations when sponsoring public awareness events related to sex discrimination and Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses how such events factor into monitoring, notice, and potential confidentiality concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive Measures and Their Definition (§106.44(g) and §106.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'supportive measures' and requires recipients to offer and coordinate appropriate supportive measures to complainants and respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists types of supportive measures, temporary measures that may impose burdens, challenge processes, disclosures of measures, and accommodations for students with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency Removal (§106.44(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Allows recipients to implement emergency removal of a respondent when there is a non-physical, serious, and imminent threat, subject to legal protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses partial removals, relation to supportive measures, interactions with other legal requirements, and scope limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Leave (§106.44(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses when recipients may place employees on administrative leave in the context of Title IX responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers employment law intersections and due process protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited Disclosures of Personally Identifiable Information (§106.44(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits improper disclosures of PII in the course of Title IX processes and clarifies privacy protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains limits and exceptions, and interaction with FERPA and other privacy statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal Resolution Process (§106.44(k))
rubrics_metrics.description: Allows recipients discretion to offer informal resolution options, with safeguards (voluntary consent, notice, facilitators, prohibitions for certain employee-student complaints).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when informal resolution is prohibited (e.g., student complaints against employee respondents), requirements for notice before offering informal resolution, and recordation of agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framework for Grievance Procedures—Due Process and Fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets a framework requiring equitable treatment of complainants and respondents, objective evaluation of relevant evidence, and protections against bias and conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses method for determining what process is due, identifying interests, bias issues, administrative burdens, and applicability across recipient types and educational levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat Complainants and Respondents Equitably (§106.45(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandates that grievance procedures treat both parties equitably, ensuring fairness, neutrality, and trauma-informed approaches as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers expectations for balanced process design and commenters' support/opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of Interest or Bias (§106.45(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits conflicts of interest or bias among individuals involved in grievance processes and contemplates models like single-investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies recusal and independence expectations and addresses comments about investigator/decisionmaker models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of Not Responsible Until Determination (§106.45(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Affirms the presumption that the respondent is not responsible until a final determination is made under grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how this presumption interacts with interim measures and public statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframes (§106.45(b)(4) and §106.46(e)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires reasonable timeframes for grievance processes and identifies expectations for prompt resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses how timeframes balance due process, administrative burdens, and varying institutional capacities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable Limitations on Sharing Information (§106.45(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Allows reasonable limits on information sharing to protect privacy while ensuring necessary participation and notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses privacy protections, more stringent privacy requests, due process concerns, First Amendment implications, and FERPA interplay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective Evaluation of All Relevant Evidence and Exclusion of Impermissible Evidence (§106.45(b)(6)-(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires objective evaluation of relevant evidence and mandates exclusion of impermissible evidence (privileged communications, treatment records, evidence about sexual history or sexual interests unrelated to the incident).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details categories of excluded evidence, rules on evidence offered to prove consent, and treatment of privileged/confidential information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Allegations (§106.45(c); §106.46(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires written notice of allegations to parties containing sufficient details to allow the respondent and complainant to prepare a response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses timing, content, and clarifications to regulatory text requested by commenters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal of a Complaint (§106.45(d); §106.46(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies circumstances for permissive or mandatory dismissal (e.g., inability to identify respondent, withdrawal, conduct not constituting sex discrimination) and notification/appeal rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers prompt and effective steps to address discrimination after dismissal and appeal procedures when dismissal occurs before respondent is notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of Complaints (§106.45(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Allows consolidation of multiple complaints where appropriate, with attention to constitutional concerns and FERPA limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains limits on consolidation and fairness considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint Investigations and Investigative Burden (§106.45(f) & (f)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes the recipient's obligation to investigate allegations and bears the investigative burden to gather relevant, not otherwise impermissible, evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes rights to present witnesses/evidence, standards for investigative thoroughness, and burdens on recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to Relevant Evidence and Opportunity To Respond (§106.45(f)(4); §106.46(e)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires equal opportunity for parties to access relevant, non-impermissible evidence and reasonable time/opportunity to review and respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses unauthorized disclosures, FERPA issues, access to investigative reports, and how evidence access is operationalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluating Allegations and Assessing Credibility (§106.45(g); §106.46(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets expectations for methods of evaluating allegations and assessing witness/party credibility, including procedures for questioning and credibility-assessment methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses Mathews balancing test, live questioning logistics, recording of meetings, methods for assessing credibility, and handling disputes over credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of Advisor, Participation and Limits (§106.46(e)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides rules for advisors (choice, role, participation restrictions) in postsecondary student-involved grievance processes, including cross-examination and live questioning contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains advisor selection, possible restrictions on advisor conduct, and how advisors factor into fairness and due process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of Proof (§106.45(h)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses which standard(s) of proof are appropriate for Title IX disciplinary or grievance determinations and discusses 'comparable proceedings'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers different standards for students and employees, commenters' directed questions, and consistency with other institutional processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination, Remedies, and Discipline Timing (§106.45(h)(2)-(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires written determinations about whether sex discrimination occurred, mandates remedies and prompt/effective steps for complainants, and that compliance with the section occurs before imposing disciplinary sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits discipline imposed solely on a determination, addresses false statements and consensual sexual activity concerns, and prescribes remedy types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals (§106.45(i); §106.46(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides for appellate review of determinations or dismissals, including permissible grounds and procedures for appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers general appeal rights, requests to expand appeal bases, and procedural standards for appellate review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live Hearings and Removal of Live-Hearing Requirement (§106.46(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Discusses live hearings' impact and explains the final rule's removal of a general live-hearing requirement while addressing circumstances where live hearings may be appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers due process, fairness, logistical impact, and commenters' suggestions on requiring live hearings in certain circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant Secretary Review (§106.47)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides for review of certain final determinations by the Assistant Secretary of Education in specified circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains scope of review and how recipients or parties may seek such review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnancy and Parental Status Protections (§106.2, §106.40, §106.57)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'pregnancy or related conditions' and 'parental status', prohibits discrimination on these bases, and prescribes responsibilities for providing information, reasonable modifications, lactation space/time, voluntary leaves, and comparable treatment to other temporary medical conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers admissions protections, timelines, staffing flexibility, lists of reasonable modifications, requirement to provide coordinator contact information, limits on documentation, interaction with other federal laws, and employee leave/lactation protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation Consistent With Gender Identity (§106.10; §106.31)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affirms that participation consistent with gender identity is covered under Title IX's nondiscrimination scope and addresses accommodations and program participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses intersection with parental rights, health care, religious beliefs, appearance codes, juvenile justice facilities, and burdens on schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retaliation (§106.71; §106.2 Definitions of Retaliation and Peer Retaliation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits retaliation against individuals participating in Title IX processes and defines elements (protected activity, adverse action, causal connection), including peer retaliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides examples of prohibited retaliation, discusses intersection with §106.45(h)(5), First Amendment concerns, and requests for clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on Informal Resolution for Certain Employee-Student Complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Bars offering informal resolution where the complainant is a student and the respondent is an employee in certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains rationale for prohibition, exceptions, and procedural safeguards when informal resolution is used elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and Data Collection (RIA and §106.8(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires retention of specific records, training materials, and reporting/monitoring data; contemplates data collection and climate surveys to assess compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses regulatory impact (costs/benefits), changes not estimated to have costs (e.g., lactation space), and how data informs monitoring burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Impact and Flexibility Analyses (RIA, RFA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contains analyses of costs, benefits, baseline assumptions, small-entity impacts, and alternatives considered for the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes modeling of increased investigations, estimates of costs to recipients, and discussion of regulatory alternatives (scope clarifications, geographic scope, educational-level distinctions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction With Other Civil Rights Laws and Statutes (FERPA, Section 504, IDEA, FLSA, state law)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains how Title IX obligations intersect with FERPA, Section 504, IDEA, FLSA (lactation protections), and state laws; clarifies preemptive and preservative effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides directed Q&A-style clarifications and examples for recipients about disclosures, confidentiality, and coordination with other statutory duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on Evidence—Privilege and Treatment Records (§106.45(b)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Excludes privileged evidence and treatment records from consideration in grievance procedures unless properly waived or otherwise permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies categories: privileged communications, evidence provided to confidential employees, treatment records, and sexual-history evidence; guidance on consent to use such materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range of Supportive Measures and Disciplinary Sanctions (§106.45(l))
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes the range of supportive measures available to parties and the spectrum of disciplinary sanctions/remedies that may be imposed if discrimination is found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses how institutions should tailor measures/sanctions to incidents, ensure proportionality, and document decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-Investigator Model and Roles in Adjudication (§106.45(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Discusses the acceptability and concerns regarding single-investigator models (investigator also making determinations) and alternatives to separate investigator/decisionmaker roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses conflict-of-interest concerns, commenters' views, and training/competency expectations if models are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extraterritorial Application and Conduct Outside Campus
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses circumstances where Title IX obligations reach conduct occurring outside the physical campus but under the recipient's program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses study abroad, off-campus events, organization-controlled buildings, and disciplinary authority reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisions on Severability, Enforcement Practices and Coordination (Miscellaneous)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes severability clause, OCR enforcement practice explanations, technical assistance, coordination among agencies, and funding for compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also covers comments outside Title IX scope, prevention strategies, and views of the Assistant Secretary.
